newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian court throws out plea by Gandhi "husband".
newsitem.headline: Indian court throws out plea by Gandhi "husband".

text.p: The daughter of India's most prominent political family is free to go ahead with her wedding next week after a judge threw out a plea by a man who claimed he was her secret husband.

Civil Judge Vipin Gupta also slapped a fine of 3,000 rupees ($84) on V. Ramakrishna Goud for filing a "malicious suit" in which he claimed marrying Priyanka Gandhi, 25, in November 1991, the Press Trust of India (PTI) news agency said.
It said Gupta ordered criminal prosecution of Goud for making false allegations.
Gandhi, often regarded as her father's political heir, had denied Goud's claim "maliciously false, concocted and outrageous," PTI said.
Gandhi was not present in the court.
She told Gupta on Tuesday that she planned to marry Delhi businessman Robert Wadhera on February 5.
Gupta on Monday threw out a plea in which Goud sought a medical examination of Gandhi which he said would prove they had married in 1991.

Goud himself was brought to Gupta's court under judicial custody relating to a separate case. He is accused of using offensive language against low-caste Hindus in his southern state of Andhra Pradesh.

After Rajiv Gandhi was killed by a woman suicide bomber in May 1991, senior leaders of his Congress party turned to his Italian-born widow Sonia Gandhi to become the party's president. But the media-shy and self-effacing Sonia Gandhi has kept largely aloof from public life.

Some newspapers have said that Priyanka Gandhi, whom they liken to her grandmother and former prime minister Indira Gandhi, was the next choice for the Congress to keep the Nehru-Gandhi dynasty in the country's political limelight.
Priyanka Gandhi has a 27-year-old brother. But Congress sources say he is not interested in politics.
